title: Pacifica Timeline Lab strategy discovery requirements
scope: A native strategic simulation and policy-search lab that generates many possible histories, searches Pacifica's adaptive decisions across uncertainty and independent actor responses, and compares distributions of several success variables. The six written cases are regression fixtures, not the search space.

interpretation.priority: The user requires strategy discovery across thousands of paths, trade-offs among several success variables, control of Pacifica only, independent other actors and no Excel runtime. Detailed mechanisms, metrics, thresholds and implementation choices remain proposed.
interpretation.release: R1 is a bounded but complete strategy-search pilot with generated paths and independent actors. A viewer or six-case calculator is a foundation milestone, not the product goal.
interpretation.acceptance: Given/when/then criteria are future verification obligations. No product acceptance test has been run by drafting this backlog.
interpretation.milestones: Focus requirements identify design or implementation work in each milestone; they do not imply that every listed criterion is complete at that stage.
interpretation.authority: product-vision.md defines the end goal and confirmed choices; requirements.md supplies scope and semantics; this file supplies statements and acceptance criteria; model-architecture.md is a provisional implementation design.

sources.description: A flexible and adaptable world model for comparing alternate timelines in a Ledger-like dashboard without proliferating Excel rows and tabs.
Compare baseline, shared-change control, and proposed CR-032A–D, using the latest repository sources pinned at run creation.
Use a separate skill to estimate and calculate the required financial quantities for each draft.
Save project work in the project repository.
Perform requirements engineering for Timeline Lab.
Current main, repository authority rules, master storyline and finance sources.
CR-032 alternatives remain separate proposed timelines; CR-032.md is the A label in the pilot.
Six frozen pilot result bundles; exact files, sizes, hashes and anchor values are recorded in fixture-manifest.json.
Separate scenario-finance skill and provisional Timeline Lab exchange contract; proposed in draft PR 7.
Pilot Excel adapter and export/validation scripts, including dated dependency and financing corrections; these are not a general-purpose engine.
The model must not be stuck on an Excel-bound execution path. All Lab calculations must be independent of Excel.
Evaluate a database-first foundation for the world model before building the dashboard; database selection remains a recommendation.

Explore thousands of generated paths and find good sequences of events using a legitimate wargame simulation and optimization over predefined success variables; do not require the user to prewrite each outcome.
Compare trade-offs among several success variables, rather than requiring a single weighted score.
Control Pacifica's decisions; other actors respond independently.
Research what professional wargames actually track before proposing success variables.
Operational simulation state, logistics, attrition, intelligence, time and adjudication. These are design precedents, not Pacifica calibration data.
Political and human factors, influence, will to fight and the purpose-dependent nature of wargame assessment.
Robust decision making, multiobjective search and implementation candidates; no framework choice proves model validity.

decisions.recommended: Discover adaptive Pacifica strategies across thousands of generated histories, compare outcome distributions and trade-offs, and inspect failures. The six cases serve as regression references.
decisions.impact: A scenario viewer or six-case calculator does not satisfy the product objective.

decisions.recommended: One author, private local browser UI and loopback API, with a native worker that also runs without a desktop on Linux.
alternatives: Private hosted application with a separately designed calculation worker
decisions.impact: Hosting and multi-user access remain open; neither option may introduce an Excel runtime dependency.

decisions.recommended: Choose a coherent pilot spanning financing/investment, diplomatic commitments and strategic readiness/sustainment, with independent actor response and endogenous outcomes.
decisions.impact: The exact action families, actors and geographic detail must be agreed after the measurement and evidence review; a universal world model is not assumed.

decisions.recommended: Benchmark a bounded 1904–1932 pilot at 100,000 trajectories in 30 minutes on 8 CPU workers and 16 GB RAM; preserve the existing UI latency targets. Treat all throughput figures as unmeasured proposals.
alternatives: Revise a target with a recorded reason and workload
decisions.impact: Profile the native core before committing to scale; report policies, futures, rollouts, fidelity and storage separately.

decisions.recommended: Stage the exact six frozen JSON bundles and their provenance in versioned private project storage. Preserve the old adapter as archival evidence; it is not an executable test dependency.
decisions.impact: This requirements PR contains metadata only. A new checkout does not yet have the six files or local adapter scripts.

decisions.recommended: Use the researched measurement catalog in product-vision.md to select a small set of objectives and constraints; preserve separate security, prosperity, fiscal, political, partnership and human-cost measures.
alternatives: Agree explicit measures, weights, boundaries and missing-data rules
decisions.impact: Final success variables, beneficiaries, thresholds, horizons and probability assumptions remain open; no composite national-power score is authorized.

decisions.recommended: Keep a native Python simulation core and a versioned data store; evaluate PostgreSQL, batch workers and columnar result artifacts after the action/actor/objective contracts and performance profile are clear.
alternatives: SQLite for an explicitly local-only product using the same model contract
decisions.impact: The database supports the model. Actor behavior, objective definitions and credible dynamics determine the design first; no infrastructure is provisioned.

decisions.recommended: Run every supported calculation natively from the first usable release; retain Excel files and existing results only as import and reference evidence.
decisions.impact: The native financial and GDP modules require upfront implementation. Missing coverage cannot be hidden by falling back to the workbook.

decisions.recommended: Compare trade-offs among several success variables with a visible estimated Pareto set; do not require a single weighted score.
decisions.impact: The user chooses among competing outcomes after inspecting distributions and risks.

decisions.recommended: Optimize Pacifica's decisions only. Other actors respond using their own objectives, observations and constraints.
decisions.impact: The optimizer cannot prescribe cooperation, select opponent actions or choose favorable random outcomes.

decisions.recommended: Review the researched measure families, choose approximately three to five objectives per experiment, and specify constraints, geography, beneficiaries, horizon and risk measures.
alternatives: Use additional objectives with explicit visualization and search implications
decisions.impact: Numerical success thresholds and acceptable risk are not yet defined; research categories are proposals, not adopted scores.

decisions.recommended: Use 1904–1932 as a bounded first decision window with annual strategic decisions and finer crisis/logistics steps where needed; retain 1846–1932 financial regression fixtures.
decisions.impact: The pilot must demonstrate strategy discovery even if geography and action families are restricted.

milestones.title: Define the strategic problem
milestones.exit: Confirm the measurement catalog, actor roles, controllable actions, observation rules, horizon, uncertainty semantics and evidence needs. Pin the six financial fixtures as engineering references.

milestones.title: Build and verify the native world kernel
milestones.exit: A bounded world advances under Pacifica and independent actor decisions; financial, sustainment, timing and information constraints are tested without Excel. Saved fixtures are reconciled separately.

milestones.title: Discover and assess strategies
milestones.exit: The search generates policies, evaluates repeated futures, estimates the trade-off frontier, tests finalists on unseen worlds and passes the documented campaign benchmark. Trivial and small exhaustive cases expose optimizer errors.

milestones.title: Deliver the strategic exploration dashboard
milestones.exit: Users define objectives, start searches, inspect trade-offs and risk, replay paths and export policies. The discovery demonstration passes; a six-case viewer alone cannot satisfy release.

milestones.title: Expand the model domain
milestones.exit: Additional regions, actor types and event families pass their own evidence and behavior checks while using the same strategy/rollout contracts.

numerical_tolerances.accounting_residuals: Apply the same declared absolute floor and relative tolerance to the maximum absolute term in the identity, rather than to its near-zero residual.
numerical_tolerances.override_policy: Metric-specific exceptions must be documented, versioned and shown in the validation report; no widening after a failure without review.
numerical_tolerances.other_numeric_kinds: Each additional metric kind requires a declared tolerance and aggregation rule before it can pass regression.

requirements.title: Pin every experiment
requirements.statement: An experiment shall pin its baseline, proposal sources, model, input data and engine versions; a new repository head shall never silently change an existing run.

acceptance.given: The six pilot bundles and a newer main commit
then: Its original hashes and results remain selected.
The newer baseline is offered as a separate version.

requirements.title: Import the six bundles
requirements.statement: The importer shall ingest pacifica.timeline-lab.scenario.v0.1 losslessly through a versioned adapter, preserving original bytes, run labels, unknown fields and provenance.

acceptance.given: The six files in fixture-manifest.json
then: Six scenario identities and 17 run records are available, with 14 distinct input hashes.
Reimport does not create duplicate identities or treat the three reused runs as independent evidence.
Unsupported schema majors fail with actionable diagnostics.

requirements.title: Define quantities explicitly
requirements.statement: Every plotted or calculated metric shall declare entity, geography, units, currency where applicable, price basis, temporal resolution, quantity kind (stock, flow, rate, ratio or index), aggregation rule and missing-value semantics.

acceptance.given: Nominal GDP, real GDP, debt and an unavailable North American GDP series
then: The user sees period USD versus 1913 USD and stock versus flow.
Unavailable values remain null with reasons.
An unsupported geographic or price-basis conversion is blocked.

requirements.title: Separate approval from calculation
requirements.statement: The interface shall keep narrative authority, input evidence, execution state, accounting validation, funding feasibility and coverage separate.

acceptance.given: A calculated conditional draft with passing accounts
then: It remains a draft with explicit conditions and MODEL quantities.
Passing accounts does not mark canon approved or political feasibility proven.
Imported canon_approved:null is treated as unassessed rather than true.

requirements.title: Fork without changing history
requirements.statement: A user shall fork any scenario version, edit a draft and save a new immutable version with parentage and a semantic change summary.

acceptance.given: A saved D reference and a fork
acceptance.when: The fork is edited and run
then: The parent and all historical results are unchanged.
The saved version records parent, author or source agent, change reason and creation time.
A later edit cannot relabel an older result as current.

requirements.title: Use dated semantic changes
requirements.statement: Changes shall target stable event, entity, parameter or instrument IDs with explicit effective periods and set, add, remove, shift or replace operations; unsupported operations shall be identified before running.

acceptance.given: A borrowing-capacity change effective from 1928
then: Years before 1928 retain the parent capacity.
The business-facing edit contains no worksheet coordinates.
The compiler reports its source mappings and unsupported effects.
Ambiguous overlapping edits in one version are rejected; an interactive conflict-resolution workflow can follow in R2.

requirements.title: Track dependencies
requirements.statement: The system shall identify downstream schedules, claims, receipts, rights and outputs affected by a change and invalidate dependent results.

acceptance.given: A loan or concession-producing event is removed
then: Repayments, interest, losses and related rights appear in the impact list.
Dependent outputs become stale until recomputed.
An unmapped material dependency yields blocked or explicitly partial coverage, never a silent inherited benefit.

requirements.title: Review rebases and conflicts
requirements.statement: Changing a parent version or combining overlays shall require explicit resolution of conflicting targets and dependent assumptions.

acceptance.given: Two overlays set the same field for overlapping years
acceptance.when: A combined version or rebase is prepared
then: The conflict names the target, periods and competing values.
No implicit last-write-wins result is produced.
The old version and results remain recoverable.

requirements.title: Handle unresolved continuations
requirements.statement: The system shall distinguish unestimated quantities from unresolved political branches and support named conditional continuations.

acceptance.given: CR-032C with its C0 completion condition
acceptance.when: A 1932 result is displayed or a new run is requested
then: C0 is visible beside the result and in exports.
D's institutions are not inherited into C.
A required unresolved quantity blocks the affected computation or produces explicitly partial outputs; it is never filled with zero.

requirements.title: Integrate the finance skill
requirements.statement: The finance skill shall produce versioned quantity proposals containing units, dates, counterparties, source evidence, derivations, bounds and dependencies for application to a scenario draft.

acceptance.given: A new spending or loan programme needing quantities
then: The proposed quantities and derivations are inspectable and editable as a batch.
A validated proposal can be applied and run as MODEL assumptions without per-cell approval prompts.
The deterministic run does not call a language model to invent replacement values.

requirements.title: Make runs reproducible
requirements.statement: Run identity and caching shall depend on resolved initial state, policy and actor-model versions, source/model/engine hashes, uncertainty specification and random-stream allocation; results shall be immutable and reproducible for identical inputs and streams.

acceptance.given: An unchanged input set and engine, then one changed parameter
then: The unchanged run reproduces values within declared tolerances and may reuse its result.
The changed parameter creates a different calculation identity.
Execution timestamps and display labels cannot cause false cache hits or replace provenance.

requirements.title: Respect time and detect cycles
requirements.statement: The engine shall evaluate dated dependencies in order and reject unconfigured same-period cycles; any iterative solver shall declare convergence criteria and failure behavior.

acceptance.given: A 1923 earthquake loan dependent on earlier accounts, and an artificial unresolved cycle
then: The dated loan is priced from valid upstream state without retaining cached downstream values.
The cycle yields a named dependency diagnostic rather than apparent success.
Every scenario and sensitivity preserves the parent before its declared divergence unless anticipation is explicitly modelled.

requirements.title: Control calculation jobs
requirements.statement: Jobs shall have queued, running, succeeded, failed and cancelled states, bounded execution, progress updates and cancellation that protects user files and applications.

acceptance.given: A long run and an unavailable worker
acceptance.when: A user starts, inspects and cancels jobs
then: A run is never shown as succeeded merely because it was submitted.
Cancellation or failure preserves the last complete result and logs the affected stage.
Cancellation stops only the owned native worker job, leaves source artifacts unchanged and cannot publish incomplete results as complete.

requirements.title: Show fresh results accurately
requirements.statement: Each view shall distinguish imported snapshots, newly calculated outputs, stale results, partial coverage and reused identical runs.

acceptance.given: A successful run followed by an unsaved input edit
then: The previous charts remain available with the exact old version and a stale label.
The UI does not redraw an edited input as a recalculated outcome.
A failed run cannot inherit a prior green validation badge.

requirements.title: Reconcile the accounts
requirements.statement: Every completed financial run shall check budget, cash sources and uses, debt stocks, claims, interest, repayments, losses and borrower-lender schedules using declared tolerances.

acceptance.given: The pilot cases and deliberately corrupted cash, debt and loan fixtures
then: All uncorrupted identities meet their documented tolerances.
Each corruption reports the entity, metric, period, expected identity and residual.
A formula-error-free workbook alone is insufficient for success.

requirements.title: Expose resource constraints
requirements.statement: For every supported module, declared funding, FX, capital, personnel and transport constraints shall produce dated gaps and explicit responses; unsupported constraint dimensions shall be marked unmodelled, and residual borrowing shall not establish feasibility.

acceptance.given: A programme with a financing or transport shortfall
then: The gap is visible at the correct entity and period.
Only a specified financing, delay or scaling rule resolves it.
A negative resource gap cannot be hidden by a generic passing accounting badge.
Coverage states which constraint dimensions are not yet modelled; passing checks cannot imply those dimensions are feasible.

requirements.title: Preserve ownership and geography
requirements.statement: The model shall distinguish sovereign, private and foreign ownership, domestic value added, partner output, legal jurisdiction and time-limited rights.

acceptance.given: Syndicated lending, Japanese production and an expired concession
acceptance.when: GDP, claims and receipts are computed
then: Treasury claims include only the public lender share.
Partner output is not added to sovereign GDP.
An absent or expired concession produces no inherited rent or asset entitlement.

requirements.title: Aggregate time correctly
requirements.statement: Annual views shall sum flows, use declared stock endpoints, recompute ratios from compatible components and retain finer schedules where material.

acceptance.given: Monthly Japanese liquidity and annual Treasury accounts
then: Monthly drawings reconcile to annual drawings without summing stock balances.
Peak liquidity needs remain inspectable even if the annual balance is positive.
The reporting horizon and any unvalued terminal obligation are explicit.

requirements.title: Compare like with like
requirements.statement: Experiments shall support baseline, control, authored and generated-policy comparisons with matched exogenous uncertainty and compatible objective definitions, while allowing endogenous outcomes and other actors' decisions to change.

acceptance.given: Baseline, control and A-D
then: The reference, years, geography, units, model and shock definition are explicit.
Matched shocks hold the chosen external inputs constant while recalculating endogenous effects.
Incompatible models or definitions require a declared comparison mapping rather than an unlabelled overlay.

requirements.title: Run bounded sensitivities
requirements.statement: The lab shall support named downside cases, finite parameter sweeps and stochastic ensembles with explicit uncertainty semantics, budgets and distinct policy/world/rollout counts.

acceptance.given: An indemnity range and D's named downside cases
acceptance.when: The user creates a sensitivity experiment
then: Each parameter setting is a reproducible run with an effective date.
Political branches, parameter ranges and structural limitations remain distinct.
Judgemental ranges and unweighted plausible futures are not labelled historical probabilities; probability estimates require an explicit distribution and show sampling uncertainty.
The planned and actual policy/world/rollout counts are shown, and the evaluation budget cannot be exceeded silently.

requirements.title: Explain differences honestly
requirements.statement: A result difference shall link to changed assumptions and dependent quantities; additive account decompositions shall reconcile, and causal contributions shall require a stated attribution method.

acceptance.given: A comparison differing in war, growth and credit assumptions
then: The changed input set and dependency path are shown.
A budget decomposition sums to its reported delta.
A total GDP difference is not attributed to a single event without controlled reruns or an explicit method.

requirements.title: Compare the main trajectories
requirements.statement: The dashboard shall provide aggregate exploration of large policy ensembles and detailed trajectory comparison for a selected subset, with synchronized year selection, levels and differences; the detailed chart limit is not a limit on search size.

acceptance.given: The six pilot cases
acceptance.when: A user selects GDP and Treasury and changes the reference
then: Nominal and real GDP, revenue, expenditure, balance, debt, cash and reserves are available.
The table and charts use the same selections and values.
A zero reference gives an undefined percentage with an explanation.

requirements.title: Inspect the timeline
requirements.statement: A timeline view shall show chosen actions, independent actor responses, sampled events, conditions and divergence points for any replayed path, linked to resulting quantities.

acceptance.given: The control and C/D forks
then: Shared changes and branch-specific changes are distinguishable.
Selecting an event exposes its source, condition, dates and effects.
Unsupported or unresolved effects are visible.

requirements.title: Edit decisions and model assumptions
requirements.statement: The editor shall distinguish Pacifica decision levers, actor-response models and uncertainty assumptions, exposing only supported fields and preventing the optimizer from treating other actors or random outcomes as controllable choices.

acceptance.given: A fork of A or D and a supported programme
acceptance.when: The user changes a quantity or effective year
then: The editor shows changed values and affected outputs before running.
Invalid units, dates and incompatible event templates cannot be submitted as valid inputs.
Unsupported narrative changes lead to an impact and estimation task instead of a misleading slider.

requirements.title: Trace any displayed number
requirements.statement: Each displayed quantity shall lead to its metric definition, scenario/run identity, formula or module, input assumptions and source references.

acceptance.given: A 1932 debt or GDP value
then: The numeric value, units and provenance match the exported result.
Inherited and newly estimated inputs are distinguishable.
Spreadsheet cell mappings, where retained, appear in the technical inspector rather than the ordinary editing flow.

requirements.title: Export a reproducible experiment
requirements.statement: Users shall export a scenario bundle, experiment manifest, selected results and validation summary with enough input and engine references to replay the calculation.

acceptance.given: A saved experiment containing new forks
acceptance.when: It is exported and reimported into an empty catalog
then: Identities, conditional labels, numbers and source hashes survive the round trip.
Exports declare unavailable external assets and worker requirements.
Chart or table exports include units, reference, period and MODEL status.

requirements.title: Protect sources and validate execution inputs
requirements.statement: Imports shall be treated as data; only registered model operations may execute, and source attachments shall remain immutable.

acceptance.given: A source workbook and a bundle containing an unexpected formula, path or script
acceptance.when: The bundle is imported or compiled
then: The source hash remains unchanged.
Untrusted executable content is rejected or retained as inert provenance.
No import, replay or calculation path invokes Excel, Office COM or a spreadsheet formula runtime; workbook formulas remain inert source evidence.

requirements.title: Validate the native engine against frozen evidence
requirements.statement: The first native engine shall reconcile all declared pilot outputs against the frozen results, pass independent accounting tests and record intentional corrections before the first usable release.

acceptance.given: The six frozen cases and the native engine on a machine without Office
then: The archived baseline evidence retains its 48,940-cell reconciliation; the new tests read frozen fixtures and never launch Excel.
All 87 annual periods and 73 pilot metrics in all 17 labelled runs, plus supplied finer schedules, are compared within declared tolerances.
Intentional corrections are explained and versioned; reproducing the baseline is not presented as historical validation.
The UI is not allowed to fall back to the workbook when a native module is missing.
Agreement with six authored paths is reported as engineering regression only and cannot certify the strategic response model or predicted probabilities.
Authored event overrides are allowed only in labelled fixture-replay mode for financial regression; they cannot force other actors' outcomes during strategy discovery.

requirements.title: Keep the initial lab private
requirements.statement: The first release shall run for a single author in a local private workspace, with no automatic upload or publication of models and drafts.

acceptance.given: A local installation with imported private artifacts
then: The default API binds to loopback and cross-origin requests are restricted.
Using a browser does not require a public deployment.
Any later hosted/shared mode has an explicit access and storage design before release.

requirements.title: Meet measured responsiveness targets
requirements.statement: On a documented reference machine, pilot import shall take at most 5 seconds at p95, cached view updates at most 250 ms at p95, and jobs shall report progress at least every 15 seconds; campaign throughput shall be benchmarked against TL-051.

acceptance.given: A release build, fixed pilot files and a declared hardware profile
acceptance.when: A benchmark of at least 20 measured trials after one warm-up is run
then: Import and interaction latency are recorded separately from simulation time.
The UI remains usable while calculation runs.
No seconds-per-reference-case target substitutes for campaign throughput; simulation, persistence and UI timings are measured separately against the declared search workload.

requirements.title: Make comparisons readable and accessible
requirements.statement: Core flows shall work by keyboard, use visible focus and textual status, and provide tables and labels that do not rely on color alone.

acceptance.given: The six-case dashboard at 1280x800 and keyboard-only interaction
acceptance.when: The user changes scenario, metric, year and reference and opens a failure
then: Every core action and error detail is reachable.
Legend labels and series styles remain distinguishable without color.
Charts have an equivalent readable data table.

requirements.title: Recover without corrupting work
requirements.statement: Draft saves and run publication shall be transactional; process interruption and concurrent tabs shall not overwrite newer versions or publish partial results.

acceptance.given: A draft and a calculation interrupted during saving, plus two editing tabs
acceptance.when: The application restarts or the second tab saves
then: The last completed version and result remain readable.
An interrupted job is marked interrupted or failed with restart guidance.
A stale version produces a conflict rather than overwriting a newer draft.

requirements.title: Register models and capabilities
requirements.statement: Each model module shall declare versioned inputs, outputs, units, state transitions, dependencies, supported events, temporal resolution and validation checks.

acceptance.given: A new loan type or cost programme implemented against the module contract
then: Its inputs enter through the schema and model registry rather than CR-number conditionals.
The editor shows only supported operations.
Its declared dependency and accounting checks run with the rest of the model.

requirements.title: Extend the world state
requirements.statement: The scenario and run contracts should extend beyond the bounded strategy-search pilot to additional regions, actor types, event families and richer demographic, industrial, trade, military-logistics and institutional modules.

acceptance.given: An additional migration or production module with two entities and a capacity constraint
acceptance.when: A new event affects that module and finance
then: Entity identities and time semantics are shared across modules.
The downstream budget and output effects use declared relationships and units.
Module coverage is explicit; absent full national accounts are not inferred.

requirements.title: Evaluate policy limits with valid denominators
requirements.statement: Targets shall specify geography, years, exceptions and numerator/denominator definitions; missing denominators shall produce unavailable checks.

acceptance.given: D's North American defence and debt targets, but only core Pacifica GDP is supplied
then: The North American targets are unavailable with a reason.
Core-GDP proxy ratios are separately labelled.
A rule starting in 1928 cannot create a failure in 1862.

requirements.title: Version the data contract
requirements.statement: The product shall define a machine-validated exchange schema, explicit migration rules and a portable result catalog independent of the Excel layout.

acceptance.given: A v0.1 pilot bundle, an upgraded bundle and an unknown future major
then: Supported migrations preserve original files and record the adapter version.
Unknown majors are rejected without changing the catalog.
The normalized contract represents entities, events, assumptions, instruments, shocks, runs, observations, checks and provenance without requiring a workbook cell address.
A database export resolves all immutable scenario inputs so the native engine can replay it without a live database connection.

requirements.title: Run without Excel
requirements.statement: Every supported Lab calculation shall run in the native engine without Excel, Office COM, an interactive desktop, spreadsheet formula evaluation or an Excel fallback.

acceptance.given: A clean supported Windows environment and a clean supported Linux environment with no Office installation
acceptance.when: The same frozen input bundle and a changed supported assumption are run through the command-line entry point
then: Both environments compute new results within declared tolerances.
No workbook application or remote spreadsheet service is invoked.
The changed input is recomputed; returning only a saved pilot result does not pass.
Missing native coverage gives an explicit unsupported result rather than a workbook fallback.

requirements.title: Persist a versioned domain model
requirements.statement: The database shall store immutable source and scenario versions, typed entities, dated events, assumptions, instruments, rights and run evidence with referential integrity and transactional publication.

acceptance.given: A baseline, two forks, a loan instrument and a later correction to an entity or assumption
acceptance.when: The versions are saved, queried, exported and restored
then: Old runs resolve to their original input revisions; correcting a shared entity cannot silently change them.
A fork stores a pinned parent and its changes without a new table or schema for that scenario.
Foreign keys and uniqueness rules reject invalid references; ambiguous time intervals are rejected by declared constraints or validation.
Original source bytes and hashes survive separately from normalized JSON payloads.
A schema migration and backup/restore preserve both identifiers and resolved input content.

requirements.title: Separate calculation from persistence and presentation
requirements.statement: The model core shall accept a complete immutable input bundle and return state trajectories, postings, checks and provenance without requiring a dashboard, live database or network service.

acceptance.given: The same resolved input bundle supplied through the database-backed application and a standalone file
acceptance.when: The native engine runs both paths
then: The calculation identity and outputs agree within declared tolerances.
All equations, module versions, dependency rules and solver settings are defined in versioned code.
Database transactions load or publish artifacts; SQL triggers do not contain economic or financial simulation equations.
Changing storage or UI code alone does not change model outcomes.

requirements.title: Separate accounting identities from economic assumptions
requirements.statement: The engine shall advance explicit opening stocks through dated flows and valuation or other changes, reconcile financial postings, and identify behavioural equations and calibration assumptions separately from accounting identities.

acceptance.given: A supported public loan, spending programme and GDP module with declared opening balances
acceptance.when: A draw, repayment, interest payment, write-down and spending-date change are simulated
then: Each covered entity's balanced postings reconcile to cash, debt and claims; cash and accrual timing are explicit.
Loan principal is a financial transaction and is not automatically public expenditure or GDP.
Debt face value, cash issue proceeds, valuation changes and creditor losses use distinct quantities and rules.
GDP, price and productivity responses identify their equations, evidence, lags and coefficients; absent responses are marked unmodelled.
Cash and stock identities can pass while economic assumptions remain uncertain and constraints remain infeasible.

requirements.title: Define success before search
requirements.statement: Each search shall pin an objective-and-constraint set defining beneficiaries, scope, units, direction, horizon, aggregation across time and futures, thresholds, and evidence/coverage requirements.

acceptance.given: Candidate welfare, security, fiscal and casualty measures
then: State variables, measures of activity and measures of desired outcomes are distinguished.
Terminal, cumulative, worst-period and risk-sensitive objectives can coexist without being added in incompatible units.
Missing fields required by the chosen objective/constraint, such as units, horizon, thresholds or input coverage, produce a clear configuration error or disabled objective.
The default output is a trade-off set; no hidden weights collapse it into one score.

requirements.title: Generate legal decisions from an action catalog
requirements.statement: The simulator shall expose parameterized Pacifica actions with preconditions, duration, costs, authority, physical limits and declared state effects, from which new paths can be generated without authored outcome prose.

acceptance.given: A decision period with insufficient transport or financing and an available diplomatic proposal
then: Infeasible or unauthorized actions are rejected or resolved by a documented alternative, without free resources.
Action completion respects delays and the current information state.
A proposal to another actor is an offer, not a guaranteed acceptance.
The catalog can produce action combinations and timing absent from all six fixtures.

requirements.title: Search adaptive policies without future knowledge
requirements.statement: The search shall optimize policies mapping Pacifica's observable history to actions, while supporting fixed plans as labelled comparators and preventing access to hidden state or future draws.

acceptance.given: Two worlds with identical observed histories until a later shock
acceptance.when: The same policy acts before and after the shock becomes observable
then: Pre-shock decisions are identical for identical information and policy randomness.
The policy may adapt after a relevant observation.
A clairvoyant comparator, if used for a bound, is explicitly labelled and excluded from implementable recommendations.

requirements.title: Represent independently responding actors
requirements.statement: Other actors shall select actions using their own versioned objectives, information, capabilities, constraints and response policies; Pacifica's optimizer shall not directly choose their actions.

acceptance.given: A Pacifica offer evaluated against two actor-response models
acceptance.when: The simulation repeats with matched external uncertainty
then: Counterparties can accept, reject, counteroffer or change commitments through declared rules.
Changing the opponent model changes outcomes where the model predicts it should.
Actor decisions and visible reasons are logged; independent agency does not require statistically independent random draws.
A centrally chosen favorable history is not presented as a Pacifica-controlled strategy.

requirements.title: Model strategic capability and sustainment
requirements.statement: The bounded pilot shall connect economics and public accounts to force availability, mobilisation, sustainment, geography/access, political support and independent actor decisions at declared resolutions.

acceptance.given: A supported crisis with reduced supplies, delayed readiness and uncertain partner access
then: Resources and travel/production time constrain feasible commitments.
Reported military capability reflects usable and sustainable forces rather than inventory alone.
Territorial control, legal sovereignty, treaty access and partner consent remain distinct.
Modern operational source categories are adapted to the historical period; unmodelled mechanisms are visible.

requirements.title: Represent uncertainty explicitly
requirements.statement: The model shall distinguish stochastic variation, uncertain parameters and alternative structural/actor models, with justified ranges, dependence assumptions and probability status.

acceptance.given: A correlated economic shock and alternative political-response models
then: Supported correlations, conditional triggers and time persistence are preserved.
Unweighted exploratory cases yield coverage/regret summaries, not asserted historical probabilities.
Probability distributions and their evidence are versioned; unsupported precision is not introduced.
Random seeds, structural-model choice and other actors' compliance are not Pacifica decision variables.

requirements.title: Evaluate policies across repeated generated futures
requirements.statement: Each policy shall be evaluated through reproducible rollouts under registered uncertainty, using separately identified random streams for search and world evolution and documented coupling for matched comparisons.

acceptance.given: A fixed policy/world design, serial execution and parallel execution
then: Rollout identities and outputs agree within declared tolerances regardless of worker scheduling.
Matched comparisons share exogenous draws where semantically valid while allowing endogenous events to diverge.
A single lucky path is not scored as the policy's expected performance.
All completed, infeasible, terminal-loss and failed evaluations remain accounted for.

requirements.title: Search a set of multiobjective strategies
requirements.statement: The optimizer shall generate and improve candidate policies, enforce constraints and maintain an estimated nondominated set across selected distributional objectives within an explicit budget.

acceptance.given: A small enumerable benchmark and a larger bounded policy family
then: The benchmark frontier agrees with exhaustive evaluation under fixed settings.
The larger search is compared with simple policies and random search under equal evaluation budgets.
Users can inspect trade-offs without a mandatory scalar score.
Outputs say best found within the declared model, policy family and budget unless a global guarantee is established.

requirements.title: Test finalists on unseen futures and actor models
requirements.statement: Finalist policies shall be reevaluated on held-out world samples and challenged against alternative actor/structural models, with explicit separation of search and assessment evidence.

acceptance.given: A policy set selected using training worlds
then: Held-out samples do not guide search selection; reuse after inspection is labelled development evidence and requires a fresh final set.
Tail loss, failure rate and sampling uncertainty are reported under the specified uncertainty model.
Unsupported rare-event claims and rank changes across assumptions are visible.
No candidate wins by omitting bankruptcy, conflict loss or simulated casualties from the result denominator.

requirements.title: Explain strategic strengths and failures
requirements.statement: The lab shall identify the decisions, constraints and conditions associated with each policy's success or failure and support controlled reruns for decision-relevant counterfactuals.

acceptance.given: A finalist with both successful and failed paths
then: The user can inspect trigger conditions, actor responses, resource bottlenecks and failure paths.
Associations from sensitivity or scenario-discovery analysis are distinguished from causal estimates.
Controlled reruns identify what changed and preserve valid matched uncertainty.
Any narrative summary is grounded in recorded actions and results.

requirements.title: Run large campaigns within a declared budget
requirements.statement: The runner shall support at least 1,000 distinct candidate policies and 100,000 complete trajectories for the bounded pilot, with preflight cost estimates, parallel execution, checkpoint/resume and per-evaluation status.

acceptance.given: A declared 1904–1932 pilot workload and an interrupted campaign
then: Reports separate unique policies, distinct behavior summaries, world samples, actual rollouts, cache hits and failures.
The proposed target is 100,000 trajectories in 30 minutes on 8 declared CPU workers and 16 GB RAM; this is unmeasured and must be validated or revised explicitly before implementation commitments.
Three full measured campaign trials after warm-up record wall time, memory, storage and model fidelity; workload reduction cannot be hidden.
Pause/resume preserves random streams and search state, and user budgets bound execution.
Workers avoid a database write for every simulation step; compact results and replay inputs remain durable.

requirements.title: Explore outcome distributions and trade-offs
requirements.statement: The dashboard shall show objective distributions, estimated Pareto trade-offs, joint target attainment, uncertainty sensitivity and selected path replays across the full campaign.

acceptance.given: A campaign with competing prosperity, fiscal and security outcomes
acceptance.when: The user filters limits and selects a policy
then: The display reveals typical, adverse and failed paths with sample counts and model conditions.
Joint target attainment is computed per rollout rather than by multiplying marginal success rates.
The user can narrow constraints, compare policy families and inspect conditional decision rules.
Reweighting uncertainty or changing a metric uses compatible raw results or queues new evaluation; incompatible results are never silently reranked.

requirements.title: Establish model credibility for its intended use
requirements.statement: The model shall maintain evidence for financial identities, physical limits, actor-response mechanisms and optimizer behavior, including independent benchmarks, ablations and model-exploitation checks.

acceptance.given: A proposed search-capable model
then: Financial parity with the six cases is separated from validation of strategic behavior.
Checks expose free resources, instant mobilisation, unsupported treaty acceptance, future-information leakage and terminal-horizon debt dumping.
Historical or other independent cases test only the mechanisms and conditions they actually support.
Results identify uncertain human factors and uncovered domains; search cannot improve rank by exploiting missing outputs.

requirements.title: Replay and export a discovered strategy
requirements.statement: A saved search result shall include policy, initial state, objective definition, actor/uncertainty models, model/engine versions, random-stream plan and traceable evaluation artifacts.

acceptance.given: A generated finalist that was not one of the six authored cases
acceptance.when: It is exported and replayed in a fresh supported environment
then: Its selected trajectories and aggregate evaluation reproduce within declared tolerances.
The event timeline identifies Pacifica actions, other actors' actions and chance outcomes separately.
The export can become a new draft narrative/scenario without implying canon approval.
Missing external assets are identified before replay.

requirements.title: Score distributions without hiding their assumptions
requirements.statement: Objective evaluation shall support means, quantiles, cumulative/path measures, tail losses and joint threshold attainment with clear probability/weight semantics, horizon treatment and missing-data rules.

acceptance.given: Two policies with similar averages but different downside and survival profiles
then: The chosen risk statistic changes their trade-off position as defined, without silently changing the raw metric.
Quantiles and tail measures report sample sufficiency; no failures are dropped.
Unweighted robustness ensembles report fractions of tested cases rather than calibrated probabilities.
Post-horizon debt, claims, depletion and continuation assumptions are reported so terminal scoring cannot hide deferred costs.

requirements.title: Demonstrate discovery without prewritten outcomes
requirements.statement: The first usable pilot shall discover and assess new adaptive strategies in a bounded domain with independently responding actors; importing and ranking six scripted histories is insufficient.

acceptance.given: A fixed initial world, action catalog, objective set and uncertainty specification with no authored future storyline
acceptance.when: The user starts a discovery campaign
then: At least 1,000 distinct candidate policies and 100,000 generated paths are evaluated within the declared benchmark or revised approved scope.
At least one conditional policy produces different action sequences after different observed shocks.
Other actors can refuse or counter a Pacifica action, changing subsequent events.
The result is an assessed trade-off set with held-out evidence and replayable successes and failures.

requirements.title: Gate metrics on usable evidence and coverage
requirements.statement: Every proposed success or state measure shall identify definition, measurement scale, source availability, module coverage and the effect of its uncertainty on decisions before being used in search.

acceptance.given: Candidate readiness, political cohesion and prosperity measures
then: Physical quantities, observable behavior and qualitative/ordinal assessments remain distinguishable.
Missing political or military data is not filled with invented precise scores.
Data collection and calibration needs are recorded; incomplete metrics are disabled or explicitly modelled assumptions.
Modern wargame categories are treated as design precedents, not empirical validation of Pacifica.
